# A grid's sortable toggle and column resize can skip headers and rows

Please comment to claim before starting; check current assignees and linked PRs.

## Context

Two grid surfaces change many children at once. When one child updates itself in the same tick, every other child keeps its old state. Both are measured in unit tests on `dev` at `87e0ae1bc4`.

**1. The header toolbar's `sortable`.** A mounted grid has the center headers `name` and `city`. One synchronous pass sets `headerToolbar.sortable = false` and `cityButton.text = 'Town'`. Afterwards `name`'s vdom carries the `neo-sort-hidden` class, but its vnode does not. The vnode is what reached the DOM, so `name` keeps its sort arrow.

**2. A column resize in the body.** One synchronous pass calls `body.updateCellPositions('name', 333)`, the call a live column resize makes on every pointer move, and changes the record of row 3. Afterwards every row's vdom gives the `name` cell `width: 333px`, but only row 3's vnode does. Rows 0–2 and 4–7 keep `200px`, so their cells stop following the header. A grid whose records stream in while a user drags a column edge hits this on every frame.

## The Problem

Both methods change their children silently, then ship them through the owner's own update at `updateDepth = 2`:
- `grid.header.Toolbar#afterSetSortable` runs `item.setSilent({sortable: value})` on every header.
- `grid.Body#updateCellPositions` writes each row's cell `style.width` / `style.left` straight into the row's vdom.

When one child's own update merges into that cycle (a header's `text` change, a row's record change), the engine builds the cycle sparse. It expands only the merged children, so every other child's silent change never reaches the DOM.

#21449 is the same class for the headers' `aria-colindex`. #19402 and #19404 fixed it at other sites.

## The Architectural Reality

- **`src/grid/header/Toolbar.mjs`, `afterSetSortable`:** a `setSilent` loop over the headers, then `me.updateDepth = 2; me.update()`. Each header's own `afterSetSortable` in `src/grid/header/Button.mjs` toggles `neo-sort-hidden` on its `cls`.
- **`src/grid/Body.mjs`, `updateCellPositions`:** loops `me.items` (the rows) and writes into `row.vdom.cn`, then `me.updateDepth = 2; me.update()`. `grid.header.plugin.Resizable#onDragMove` calls it on every move.
- **Design authority:** the JSDoc of `denseUpdate` in `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs`: *"True for one update cycle: the owner changed descendants silently within its `updateDepth`, so the cycle ships that subtree whole instead of sparse, even when children merge into it."*
- **The sparse rule:** `VdomLifecycle#executeVdomUpdate`, in `const ids = component.updateDepth !== 1 && !component.denseUpdate ? mergedChildIds : null`.

## The Fix

In both methods, set `me.denseUpdate = true` beside `me.updateDepth = 2`, so the cycle ships every child whole. `component.Base#hide()` does the same for its parent. Patching only these two lines makes both measurements above pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A unit test toggles `headerToolbar.sortable` while one header's own update (for example a `text` change) runs in the same pass. It asserts that every header's **vnode** `className` includes `neo-sort-hidden`. It fails on `dev` and passes with the fix.
- [ ] A unit test calls `body.updateCellPositions(dataField, width)` while one row's record changes in the same pass. It asserts that every rendered row's **vnode** cell for that field has the new width. It fails on `dev` and passes with the fix.
- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/grid/HeaderButtonSortable.spec.mjs` and `test/playwright/unit/grid/ColumnResizeCellSync.spec.mjs` stay green.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` stays green.

## How to write the tests

Model them on `test/playwright/unit/grid/AriaRegions.spec.mjs`. Its `createGrid()` mounts a grid with rows and `allowVdomUpdatesInTests`, and #21449's last test in that file has the same shape. Avoid three traps:
- **Read the vnode, never the vdom.** The vdom always holds the new value, so a vdom assertion passes on `dev` too.
  - A header's vnode carries `className`.
  - A row's cells are `row.vnode.childNodes`; find the one whose `attributes['data-field']` is the field, and read its `style.width`.
- **Reset the owner's depth first.** The grid setup can leave an owner at `updateDepth = -1`, which always ships whole and hides the defect. Call `await headerToolbar.promiseUpdate()` (or `await body.promiseUpdate()`) once before the change; a settled cycle resets the depth to its default.
- **Make the merge happen in the same synchronous pass.** Change the record with `store.get(3).city = 'Changed'` right after `updateCellPositions()`, with no `await` in between.

## Out of Scope

- `Toolbar#afterSetUseTriStateSorting` follows the same pattern, but a header's `useTriStateSorting` changes no vdom (it is read at click time), so nothing can be lost there.
- The header filter field's `removeDom` in `grid.header.Button`. It is unmeasured, so no claim is made.

## Related

- #21449: the same class for `aria-colindex`; its PR carries the test template.
- #19402, #19404: the same fix at other sites.
- #19798: made `sortable` reach every header region, a different defect.
